statusDetail: Complete 58-check atomic audit. Requests redirected to the UK BBC experience for this audit location.

page.framework: React/Next-like homepage plus BBC MPA templates
page.notes: Public editorial/media service. Representative homepage, section, article, search and 404 templates were covered. Authenticated account, playback, weather location, iPlayer/Sounds, children/education and checkout-like journeys were not covered because they are separate products or require broader consent/auth/location scope.

paths.description: Homepage and global navigation; represents the main editorial landing template.
News section listing; represents a section/index template and promotional chrome.
Current news article; represents editorial detail content and share metadata.
Search results for “climate”; represents the primary search form and result-list journey.
Deliberately invalid URL; represents HTTP failure and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt its main surfaces to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white page with white cards; only loading placeholders change, while body and content surfaces do not retint.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use preference-aware surface/text tokens, for example light-dark(), while preserving BBC brand colors.

findings.summary: Long-running animations remain active when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirmed matchMedia(...reduce) and found 18 running animations, each with an 8,000 ms duration. CSS contains reduced-motion rules, but the active loading animations were not suppressed.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, stop non-essential skeleton/auto-advance animation and replace it with a static state or near-instant transition.

findings.summary: Fresh visitors encounter content-obscuring overlays before they can read.
findings.evidence: The homepage and mobile search screenshots show a fixed cookie panel covering roughly half the viewport. The article screenshot adds a centered sign-in modal over the cookie layer and dims the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep necessary consent compact and non-obscuring where legally possible, avoid stacking prompts, delay account promotion until contextual intent, and ensure immediate light-dismiss.

findings.summary: The cookie overlay is custom fixed chrome rather than an appropriate dialog/popover primitive.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe reported zero dialog and zero popover elements while the screenshot and interaction probe show the cookie UI as a fixed SECTION.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for genuinely modal consent or popover for transient promotion, with native focus management, Escape/light-dismiss behavior, and no stacked top-layer surfaces.

findings.summary: Cold mobile performance is well outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse scored performance 0.34, with FCP 5.8 s, LCP 14.0 s, TBT 1,700 ms, and time to interactive 23.2 s. A separate trace measured LCP 2.94 s and 64 ms TBT, confirming variable but non-good LCP.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image, shorten dependency chains, and defer non-critical personalization, analytics, and media code until after primary content.

findings.summary: Heavy script execution blocks the main thread on a cold load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 1,700 ms TBT and 710 ms maximum potential input delay. The raw-CDP trace independently found three long tasks (longest 81 ms).
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, schedule non-critical work after interaction/idle, and remove or lazy-load scripts that do not support the initial viewport.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a large script surface with substantial unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 99 scripts and 1.12 MB transferred JavaScript. Lighthouse estimated 283 KiB unused JavaScript, including player, analytics, and website bundles over 50% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split player and personalization code, conditionally import analytics/media dependencies, and remove duplicate legacy bundles from the homepage.

findings.summary: The homepage heading hierarchy skips levels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.99 but failed heading-order: the lead story is an H3 directly under the H1 without an intervening H2. The DOM heading probe corroborates this structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Use headings to reflect document hierarchy, introducing the appropriate section H2 before story-card H3 headings.

findings.summary: Several visible links have touch boxes below common minimum target guidance.
findings.evidence: The target-size probe found repeated “View more” links only 22 px high and a comments-count link 16.25×24 px. Mobile reflow itself had no horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand the clickable area of compact links to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 where space allows, without changing visual text size.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP is absent and several cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no Content-Security-Policy. The cookie audit found five first-party cookies with Secure=false and SameSite=None; Lighthouse also logged CSP/cookie inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive report-only then enforced CSP, and set Secure plus an intentional SameSite value on every cookie sent over HTTPS.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are missing or weak.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN, but Permissions-Policy is absent, CSP/frame-ancestors is absent, and Referrer-Policy remains no-referrer-when-downgrade.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, CSP frame-ancestors, and a stricter Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

findings.summary: The initial page has a broad personalization and measurement footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker primitive observed 14 non-main origins, including Optimizely, Piano, Chartbeat and Cxense. The HAR attributes 206 of 207 requests and 1.89 MB to origins different from www.bbc.com (including BBC asset domains), with external personalization scripts among the largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit vendor necessity, load experimentation/measurement only after consent and intent, batch events, and treat BBC-controlled asset domains separately from external vendors in budgets.

findings.summary: A non-JavaScript crawler receives materially different, incomplete page semantics.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 37% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML; the raw response lacked the rendered title and H1, although it was not an empty JS shell and retained substantial text.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render stable title, H1 and primary editorial modules so core semantics and content match before hydration.

findings.summary: Image delivery is responsive but still wastes bytes through legacy and oversized candidates.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 100/100 images delivered as JPG/PNG, 11 over 2× displayed width, three without dimensions, and six below-fold images not lazy-loaded. All images did expose srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Negotiate AVIF/WebP from the image CDN, tighten sizes/srcset selection, add dimensions, and lazy-load non-critical below-fold images.

findings.summary: Repeated menu interaction is associated with large retained-heap growth and needs controlled leak investigation.
findings.evidence: A fresh baseline heap summary reported 126,462 nodes / 10.3 MB self size; after ten menu open/close attempts a fresh-session post snapshot reported 794,217 nodes / 47.0 MB. Different hydration timing can explain part of this delta, so this is a low-confidence leak signal, not a proven leak trace.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one controlled session after hydration and GC, then trace retainers for growing closures, timers, menu DOM and personalization caches.

taskList.title: Remove stacked on-load prompts and use semantic top-layer primitives
Cut initial JavaScript, long tasks and LCP dependency chains
Enforce CSP, secure cookies and least-privilege browser policies
Reduce consent-time third-party measurement and personalization
Honor dark scheme and reduced motion preferences
Server-render stable homepage title, H1 and primary content
Modernize responsive image formats and sizing
Repair heading hierarchy and compact touch targets
Run a controlled same-session memory leak trace
